points.description: States that the number of operations in the best case is N, the length of the array (equivalent wording such as 'linear, O(n)' or 'n comparisons/operations' earns the mark).
States that the best case is when the array is already sorted (equivalent wording such as 'input already in ascending order' earns the mark).

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) require both the count of N operations and the scenario of an already-sorted array. Each point is all-or-nothing, so there is no partial credit. Answers that give the worst case (reverse-sorted array) or an average-case count instead of the best case should not earn P2 or P1.
